$comment: The GitHub Copilot CLI stack. The ladders are the claude set's, inherited by name so the two cannot drift; the runner is Copilot's own.
$why: Operator, 2026-09-27: calls to GitHub Copilot must carry the ladder's settings and work with retry and self-heal, with 'models same as claude map to those if available'. The pipeline keeps claude-set model ids everywhere it records a model (PRD, rung state, overrides); the copilot plugin maps an id to the one Copilot serves at the moment of the call (plugins/providers/copilot/copilot-models.js, read from Copilot's own catalog), so nothing upstream of the call changes and no other set can be affected.

inheritFrom.$whyOnlyThese: The claude RUNNER is not inherited: a set declaring both runners makes `claude` routable, and resolve_primary_provider could route a copilot run to it.

finalFallback.$why: The claude set's fallback model, served by copilot: the same second answer after ladder exhaustion, on this stack.

copilot.$why: The GitHub Copilot CLI, non-interactive: the prompt on stdin, JSONL events on stdout. Every flag below was checked against `copilot --help` (1.0.85) and exercised against a recording stub on 2026-09-27.
copilot.$whyAlwaysFlags: --output-format json: the verdict of a call is in its JSONL (session.error, result.exitCode) — the CLI exits 0 on an unknown model, an unsupported effort and a 402 alike. NO --no-auto-update (removed 2026-09-28): it does not merely skip a download — it makes the loader run the npm-bundled build (1.0.18 here) instead of the current one (1.0.85), and the bundled build refused claude-sonnet-5 as "not available" on the first live call. A run uses the CLI the operator uses. --disable-builtin-mcps: the GitHub MCP server is a tool surface no seam was granted. --allow-all-tools: non-interactive mode requires it; the seam's grant narrows the set with --available-tools.
copilot.$whyNoFlags: --model and --reasoning-effort are not plain setting-to-flag copies: the model is mapped to Copilot's id and the effort passed only when Copilot's catalog lists it for that model (an unsupported one is an error the CLI exits 0 on). The copilot plugin applies both through plugins/providers/copilot/copilot-models.js.
copilot.$whyNoTurnCap: maxIterations is deliberately absent: Copilot's agent loop is its own and the CLI offers no turn cap.
copilot.$whyNoOutputCap: maxOutputTokens is deliberately unmapped: the CLI has no flag for a Copilot-served model's output cap (only BYOK's COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS). A response cut at the cap is continued by the CLI itself (proven against the stub: finish_reason=length → it asks again).
copilot.$whyToolNames: The Copilot CLI's own tool names, read from the tool list it sends the model (spike, 2026-09-27): view, glob, grep, web_fetch, bash, create, edit — and more (task, sql, skill, …) that no seam grant names, so a granted seam never receives them.
